item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q022_colg_crya_remote_homology","answer":"In SCOPe 2.04 the ColG collagenase collagen-binding domain from 1nqd and the Cry3A C-terminal domain from 1dlc were not classified as homologous beyond both being all-beta proteins: 1nqd chains A/B were b.23.2.1, in the CUB-like fold b.23 and the Collagen-binding domain superfamily b.23.2, whereas the Cry3A C-terminal domain d1dlca1, 1dlc A:500-644, was b.18.1.3, in the Galactose-binding domain-like fold b.18 and superfamily b.18.1. In current SCOPe 2.08, 1dlc A:500-644 remains the delta-Endotoxin C-terminal domain family b.18.1.3, but ColG has been moved to the same b.18 fold and same homology-implying b.18.1 Galactose-binding domain-like superfamily as a new separate family, b.18.1.36 / Collagen-binding domain, SUNID 267607; the 2.08 b.18.1 homology record has homology_implied_by_level=true with homology_scope=\"sf\". The relationship therefore changed from a structural resemblance placed in different folds/superfamilies in 2.04 to a remote common-ancestry call at superfamily level in 2.08, not to membership in the same family or the same close functional group. The specific structural/external support recorded by SCOPe is the 2.08 ColG family annotation, which cites PubMed 17977833 as describing likely homology among ColG d1nqdb_, Cry4Ba d1w99a3, and the Clostridium perfringens enterotoxin C-terminal domain d2quoa_; d1w99a3 is itself in the same b.18.1.3 delta-endotoxin C-terminal family as Cry3A d1dlca1, while d2quoa_ is in the neighboring CPE C-terminal family b.18.1.37. Functionally, these are receptor/ligand-binding beta-sandwich C-terminal or collagen-binding modules, but their molecular targets and source proteins differ: 1nqd is a Clostridium histolyticum collagen-binding domain, 1dlc A:500-644 is only the C-terminal domain of a Bacillus thuringiensis Cry3A toxin, and 1dlc’s other two domains are b.77.2.1 and f.1.3.1.
